numerical_failure.affected_api: pandas.core.window.rolling.Rolling.cov and pandas.core.window.rolling.Rolling.corr (Cython helpers remove_cov and remove_corr in pandas/_libs/window/aggregations.pyx)
numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Once a rolling window contains no valid pairs (e.g. due to NaN values), the running mean becomes 0/0 -> NaN in remove_cov/remove_corr, and all subsequent overlapping windows return NaN, including windows that should be valid (e.g. i=3 returns NaN for cov and corr).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Subsequent windows should return correct values; for the reproducer x=[1.0,10.0,20.0,30.0], y=[1.0,NaN,20.0,30.0], x.rolling(2).cov(y) at i=3 should be 50.0 and x.rolling(2).corr(y) at i=3 should be 1.0.
trigger_conditions: A rolling window's valid-pair count drops to 0 (e.g. NaN values in y or x within the window)
Rolling cov or corr with overlapping subsequent windows
Window size 2 with NaN in one series, as in the reproducer

input_output_examples.input: x = pd.Series([1.0, 10.0, 20.0, 30.0]); y = pd.Series([1.0, np.nan, 20.0, 30.0]); x.rolling(2).corr(y)

oracle_clues: PR body states a brute-force per-window reference was used over 2000 randomized trials with 0 mismatches after the fix
Reproducer comments give expected values 50.0 (cov) and 1.0 (corr) at i=3
Whatsnew entry: returning NaN for all later windows once a window contained no valid pairs (GH#65739)

category_specific_evidence: NaN enters via the NaN value in y at index 1 (b = [1.0, nan, 20.0, 30.0]), which makes the valid-pair count drop to 0 for one window.
remove_cov/remove_corr divided by nobs without a nobs==0 guard; when the valid-pair count hits 0 the running mean becomes 0/0 -> NaN, which poisons subsequent overlapping windows.
The instability-recompute check fabs(old_ssqdm_xy)*InvCondTol > fabs(ssqdm_xy[0]) evaluates False when ssqdm_xy is NaN, so the NaN state never clears.

Correct handling per the patch: guard the Welford downdate with if nobs[0]:, and when nobs reaches 0 reset mean_x, mean_y, ssqdm_xy (and ssqdm_x, ssqdm_y in remove_corr) to 0 and set numerically_unstable to False.
Expected results for the reproducer: rolling(2).cov gives [NaN, NaN, NaN, 50.0] and rolling(2).corr gives [NaN, NaN, NaN, 1.0].
The patch was verified against a brute-force per-window reference over 2000 randomized trials with NaN gaps, with 0 mismatches.
reproduction_risks: The passages do not involve +/-inf, signed zero, or subnormals; the NaN here is a missing-value NaN that produces 0/0 in the running mean, not an IEEE special-value propagation test for those other categories.
Test expectations use assert_series_equal, whose float tolerance is not stated in the passages.
The reproducer depends on the pre-fix code path being reached (a window whose valid-pair count drops to 0 followed by overlapping windows).

provenance.value: pandas.core.window.rolling.Rolling.cov and pandas.core.window.rolling.Rolling.corr (Cython helpers remove_cov and remove_corr in pandas/_libs/window/aggregations.pyx)

Once a rolling window contains no valid pairs (e.g. due to NaN values), the running mean becomes 0/0 -> NaN in remove_cov/remove_corr, and all subsequent overlapping windows return NaN, including windows that should be valid (e.g. i=3 returns NaN for cov and corr).

Subsequent windows should return correct values; for the reproducer x=[1.0,10.0,20.0,30.0], y=[1.0,NaN,20.0,30.0], x.rolling(2).cov(y) at i=3 should be 50.0 and x.rolling(2).corr(y) at i=3 should be 1.0.
